messages:
Sam (AE): Heads-up — Large finance customer asking for Private deployment. Requirements: no SNAT for client flows, fixed egress IPs for allowlisting, and a contractual burst window (2x baseline for up to 15m). Also need a short vendor statement for their security questionnaire. Any immediate blockers?
Nora (SE): If they insist on L4 source preservation we should push TGW or VPC peering. PrivateLink only preserves identity at L7 via headers (X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP).
Olga (Customer): TGW is allowed but cross-account attachments require our change control + MFA on route updates. We cannot accept any in-VPC NAT that rewrites src IP.
Kofi (NetOps): Operational notes:
- For true 5-tuple preservation: TGW attachment or peering + route tables pointing to our connector subnets; no NAT anywhere on the path.
- For static egress IPs: reserve a pool of EIPs attached to dedicated egress instances or use BYOIP. On-demand EIPs are risky for bursts (quotas).
- Disable source/dest check on any routed EC2 instances we deploy.
Elena (Solutions Eng): Short allowlist snippet for their infra team:
```
- Destination: <connector CIDR list we will provide>
- Ports: TCP 443 (mandatory), TCP 80 (health checks only)
- Routes: route table entries to TGW attachment / peering for connector CIDRs
- DNS: allow outbound to customer resolver; fallback to 1.1.1.1 only if approved
```
Nora (SE): Pricing/SLA: connector uptime SLA we can include. Burst throughput SLA requires Dedicated reserved capacity + contractual addendum (pre-warmed nodes and reserved EIPs). Ballpark: baseline cluster for 300 rps ~$10k/mo; burst addon ~25-35% depending on region/redundancy. Finance to confirm.
Olga (Customer): We need a one-paragraph vendor response for our questionnaire explaining connectivity options and where client IPs show up in logs.
Elena (Solutions Eng): Draft paragraph: "Redwood Private supports Transit Gateway attachments, VPC peering, and Interface VPC Endpoints. To preserve transport-layer client IPs, customers should use TGW or VPC peering and avoid SNAT in the path. If Interface Endpoints are used, Redwood can surface client identity at the application layer via X-Forwarded-For headers. Static egress IPs are provided via reserved EIP pools or dedicated egress instances; BYOIP options available in select regions. Logs containing client IPs can be forwarded to customer-managed storage (S3/Kinesis) or retained in Redwood-managed encrypted stores per contract and KMS requirements."
Kofi (NetOps): Test runbook items to validate on their side: traceroute/tcpdump to our connector EIP to confirm src preservation, curl latency checks, and MTU tests to check for fragmentation.
OpsBot: Preflight ticket created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/PRIV-2024 (includes TGW playbook, EIP reservation steps, and runbook).
Sam (AE): Next steps: 1) Elena to send polished questionnaire paragraph + allowlist template by EOD. 2) Kofi to start EIP quota request. 3) Schedule technical validation call Tue 9am PT with customer's network/security.
Olga (Customer): Tue 9am PT works, thanks. One more: audit requires evidence that logs with client IPs are only stored in-region and encrypted with our KMS if possible. Can you accommodate?
Kofi (NetOps): Yes — we can support customer-managed KMS for Redwood-managed buckets under enterprise terms; we'll document in arch diagram.
Sam (AE): Great thread — will create the invite and attach the preflight ticket. :thumbsup:
